Flag tested by the restart shortcut scan and fire-release path. Tower setup copies it to $66 when entering through $82EF.

Next read index for the third title sequence, used by the reader at $391B.
Counter advanced by the title interrupt hook and reset before stepping the three music streams.

Reads one byte of the first title sequence using the current base operand and the event index in Y.
Low operand byte of the indexed base used to read title voice 1's stream.

Fetches a byte of the second title sequence at the current Y index.

Clears $3911, the flag tested by the title loop before processing the sequence.

Source sprite records 0 to 15 for the mirroring pass. Each record occupies 64 bytes including one padding byte.
Source sprite records 16 to 31. Each group of three bytes holds the next row of one 24-by-21 shape.
Source frames 32 to 47. The mirroring pass alternates the multicolour and single-bit byte-reversal tables between the two records of a pair.
Source frames 48 to 63 in the two-record layout read by $AD21.
The final ten source records read by $ACE5. The next range beginning at $5280 is a destination for generated or copied frames.
First sixteen slots of the sprite frame buffer. Title, message and play setup choose which patterns occupy it.
Sprite buffer records 16 to 31, copied from $E400 in the base setup and rewritten when mirrored frames are prepared.
Sprite buffer records 32 to 47, copied from $E800 in the base setup.
Sprite buffer records 48 to 63. The load at $B44B ends at $627F. The mirroring loop can continue past that point.
Final ten destination records of the 74-frame mirroring pass from $ACE5.
Eight 64-byte sprite slots for pointers $94-$9B in VIC bank $4000. Includes the blank frame $9A used to hide objects.
Scratch page cleared by $BCEF during player sprite initialization.
First 128 eight-byte patterns of the character set selected by $B893 for the top of the display.
Final 128 patterns selected by the same $6800 VIC character-set base.
Enters the C64 build through $8017. The immediate byte at $8001 is also read as the platform selector by memory banking and VIC initialization.
The immediate operand of the C64 entry stub is also the flag read by the code supporting two banking paths.
Powers of two from $01 to $80. Code can select a single bit by index.
Complements of the eight masks at $8005, indexed in the same bit order.
Countdown set to two after tower initialization. Both the tower and interlude paths consult it before proceeding with their scene updates.
Starting tower index used by the player-progress initializer. The shortcut scan at $826F installs its selected index here.
Configures the processor port when the platform byte is set, initializes the engine and SID, sets the one-player and sound flags, then enters the title setup at $803E.
Resets the stack to $FE, clears the byte at $170A and runs the title-screen setup before entering the game selection loop.
Calls the selection handler at $842E and restarts the title setup on carry clear.
Resets the active player's extras to zero and technique to BCD $0100. Clears the pending interlude flag and saves the progress mask before entering tower setup.
Saves the player's position and view around the finish bonus panel, then prepares the collapse scene and resumes the saved positions.
When the startup guard at $8015 is clear, reads play-time keyboard commands including the shortcut that returns to title, setting or clearing flags at $1709-$170A.
Address operand of the increment of the keyboard shortcut index at $8217.
Continues the keyboard scan with the first key in matrix column 2 after the preceding pair has been tested.
High byte of the final keyboard scan call. When its key is pressed the branch at $8269 takes the restart path.
Stores the keyboard shortcut index from $827D in $8016, resets the stack and input latch, and jumps into the new-game setup.
Number of tested keyboard shortcuts that preceded the first pressed key in the scan at $8209.
Generates display character data, decodes the tower selected by $4A and initializes player, object, shot, and pending floor state.
Low operand byte of the call to clear the four tower object slots. The following setup resets the shot and initializes the three display values at $2D-$2F.
Immediate phase offset $24 used to compute the initial view angle in $47 relative to the player. The following loop draws the tower, swaps pages and stages sprites.
Low byte of the address of the initial render-pass counter at $1703. After the decrement, setup clears the transition state and chooses the sprite entry mode.
Restores the character-set backup and initializes the scrolling background, sprite frames, submarine, fish slots and screen before the interlude.
Polls joystick and updates player, destructible tiles, projectiles and objects. Builds a back buffer, waits for display synchronization, swaps buffers and refreshes object sprites.
Compares the current height to the previous awarded watermark and advances the watermark while adding $10 of BCD score per step.
Polls the stick, updates the submarine and fish slots, draws the background, waits for the raster tick and swaps screen pages before sprite and contact updates.
Low byte of the call to update the submarine scene's fish. The remaining calls stage fish sprites, refresh the status display and check contacts.
One tower index per player. Bit 7 marks a submarine interlude pending before the indexed tower.
One byte per player with one bit per tower. The turn selection routine skips a player whose byte is zero.
Sets both saved tower indices from $8016 and gives both players the full eight-bit tower mask.
Copy of the selected player's mask shifted out into individual progress flags by $8479.
Chooses the live player for this turn, restoring their tower index and eight separate tower flags. Carry clear returns to the title when neither eligible player has a nonzero tower mask.
Reads the player count and selects whose progress to check. In two-player mode the player index is toggled and can be toggled back if the other mask is zero.
Relative displacement to the pending-interlude path at $8463. Both paths set the tower index and unpack the selected player's mask into eight flags.
Loop branch to unpack all eight saved progress bits. Carry reports whether a player with a live mask was found.
Packs the eight per-tower flags in $DC-$E3 into the current player's mask and saves the tower index along with the sign flag from $1704.
Zeros the current player's tower mask in $841A indexed by $51.
Sets the tower progress mask indexed by the current player at $51 to zero.
Clears the current tower's flag and advances the tower index in $4A and the current player's saved index.
Zero-terminated message records for the intro, tower names, results, credits, sound and player options. Values $01-$0F within a record select text colour.
Printable part of the PLAYER ONE record, following its colour control byte.
Name record for the first tower, read through the first pointer at $86BE.
Suffix of the first tower's name in the record starting at $84F4.
Name record for tower 2.
Name record for tower 3.
Name record for tower 4.
Name record for tower 5.
Name record for tower 6.
Name record for tower 7.
The final tower name, EDGE OF DOOM, followed by the two lines introducing the fish bonus.
Offset into the NO LIVES LEFT message record. The following strings describe completion and its bonus.
High digit of the upper BCD time byte, converted to a printable character by the result panel builder.
Low digit of the upper BCD time byte in the result message.
Start of the technique line in the tower-completion panel.
High digit of the active player's technique tally, formed from $5D plus the ASCII zero code.
Middle digit of the technique tally, extracted from the high nibble of the player's byte at $5C.
Updatable numeric cells near the end of the technique line and the start of the extras row.
High digit of the player's extras tally, formed from the byte at $61.
Middle digit of the extras tally, extracted from the high nibble of the player's byte at $60.
Tail of the EXTRAS row and part of the mission success and credit text block.
Tail of the title's mission heading followed by the author-introduction and author-name records.
Copyright record and the two player-count option captions, followed by the first sound-option colour byte.
Sound option captions and the time-limit message, followed by the beginning of the high-score heading.
Tail of the high-score heading followed by the two lines that prompt for the player's initials.
Eight little-endian pointers to the names that appear when entering a tower, indexed by twice the tower number.
First high pointer byte in the little-endian table of tower names.
Seven remaining tower-name pointers after the Tower of Eyes word. The first word here points to the Realm of Robots caption.
X coordinates for the eight tower preview icons, written to the eight VIC sprite position registers.
Common vertical coordinate used by the eight tower preview sprites.
Draws the entering message and the selected tower name, updates the player legend and sets eight sprites for the tower preview before waiting.
Displays the game over and lives message for the current player, with its associated effects and delay.
Prepares the message scene, plays the time-out sound sequence, writes the active player and TIME LIMIT UP, then waits.
Draws the congratulations and mission completed messages and tries to enter initials after the timed display.
Draws the active player legend and the two centered lines introducing the fish bonus scene, then waits for a raster or joystick transition through $8B51.
Pitch parameter passed in Y to the results sound call. The panel builder lowers it by two on each divider expiry.
Divider countdown for the bonus panel's pitch change. The update resets it to four.
Draws the completion panel, subtracts the remaining timer and then other bonus counters in BCD steps, and awards score as it updates each displayed value.
Converts the remaining time and the two player-selected bonus counters to decimal characters in the three result messages and requests a pitch derived from the bonus state.
Title view index. Reset to zero on entry and toggled by subtracting it from one when the view countdown expires.
Countdown to switch between the title views, reloaded with $C8 by $8AB6.
Title menu input latch initialized on entry and used by the option input path.
Prepares two title sprites from data at $EE00 and $EF00, alternates the title and score views using the counter at $89BE, reads player and sound options through the keyboard matrix and exits on fire.
Draws the one-player or two-player option then the sound on or sound off option according to $50 and $67.
Eight X coordinates for the sprite strip drawn by $8AFF.
Common Y coordinate of the eight sprites in the title strip.
Assigns sprite pointers $4A-$51 to both screen pages and positions eight sprites using $8AF6 and their common Y at $8AFE.
Resets the SID, initializes a black display, clears the scene-dependent display state and refreshes status graphics for a message.
Remaining display ticks for the current timed message. The input loop can return early after a fresh fire press.
Waits for the raster tick, swaps screen pages and then enters the timed message wait with the original A value.
Uses A as a count of display ticks. A fresh fire press ends the wait early after release.
Polls the stick until the decoded fire byte $26 is zero.
Selects the message pointer using the active player at $51 before drawing it.
Returns after drawing player two's caption. The score move loop uses this address as a biased base and reads the records that follow with a nonzero index.
Four seven-byte score records. The first byte is the least significant packed decimal pair and the final three bytes are initials.
Second packed decimal pair in the first high-score record. The renderer emits the score bytes in reverse significance order.
Third packed decimal pair in the high-score record format.
Most significant packed decimal pair, printed first for each high-score entry.
First character of the displayed initials in the seven-byte high-score record.
Second character of the recorded initials, read by the renderer at $8C9A.
Third character of the first entry's initials. Three more seven-byte score and initials records follow.
Draws the high-score heading and sends the table's rows to $8C67.
Offset of the selected initials character in its high-score record. The entry screen advances it from 4 to 7.
Acts on a score admitted by $8CB9. Initializes the initials to A and two spaces, cycles a letter with signed vertical input, and confirms each letter with fire.
Sets the text position and colour and prints the selected record's packed score digits and initials through the two-cell writer.
Draws each half of A as a decimal glyph by adding ASCII zero before calling the text routine.
Masks to a single digit and maps it to the selected character pair through $A987.
Destination index at which the seven-byte high-score shift loop stops.
Compares the selected player's score to the high-score records and returns the entry pointer if the score qualifies.
Starts the player at angle 4 and height 8, derives the view height, sets the facing bit and resets action, leave-scene and input state.
Saved pre-movement player angle. A blocked angular motion restores this byte to $C6.
Adds the motion delta to the player angle and uses the geometry probe to reject collisions.
Saved low byte of the player's height, restored on a blocked vertical step.
Saved high byte of the player's height, restored alongside the low byte at $8D77.
Adds the signed delta in A to the 10-bit height at $C7-$C8. If the collision check sets carry it restores the old height. A negative high byte exits through $93E4.
Calls the directional support test and applies its delta only if the player supplies no horizontal input.
Dispatch destinations stored minus one. The routine at $8DD4 pushes high then low from the indexed pair, so RTS adds one and enters the selected handler.
High byte of the first biased return address in the player-state dispatch table.
In the eligible mode, suppresses a held fire press after its first poll using $27. Selects a handler by pushing the return address encoded at $8DC0 for state $CD.
Clears $CD and its phase counter $CC, returning the dispatcher to state 0.

Tests geometry under the player, then chooses a state for the detected surface. In the ordinary branch, direction and fire initiate a jump while fire without direction initiates the shot. Vertical input can try lift or doorway code.
Sets player state 3 and clears its animation phase. The handler at $8E9E completes seven frames and reverses the facing bit in $CB.
Selects one of two 7-entry sequences from $9021 by facing, updates $CE, and flips the facing bit after the seventh step.
Magnitude of the downward probe in the forced-step state. A blocked probe reduces it before trying a shorter one.
Angular delta for the forced step. The motion routine clears it if the attempted movement hits geometry.
Count of angular attempts in the initial forced-step phase. The transition test compares it with two.
Total forced-step update counter, incremented at the state handler's entry.
Starts the stationary variant of state 2. Nearby entries choose the signed push direction and animation before sharing the stores at $8EF2.
Advances state 2 with its working counter and the motion parameters selected by the entry path at $8EC3-$8EF2.
Signed horizontal motion captured when starting a jump, then passed to the angular collision routine on each step.
Working signed vertical delta for the jump, saved before the collision probe and retried in shorter steps when possible.
Jump mode. The vertical step selector checks its sign bit to choose the alternate displacement table.
Jump phase limit supplied by the jump entry. The animation compares its state phase with this byte.
Signed height changes indexed by jump phase when bit 7 of $8F7B is clear. The sequence begins at +3 and passes through zero before descending.
Signed height changes read by $8FE0 when bit 7 of the jump mode byte at $8F7B is set.
Sets state 1, captures the stick direction at $8F79, resets the jump phase and its working values, and requests effect 9.
Runs the jump using its phase counter and the direction saved by $8F90. Checks vertical and horizontal motion as it progresses.
Carries the result of the vertical collision test into the forced-step decision. A clear carry takes the generic reset entry at $8ECA.
High byte of the reset target in the jump at $9015. The alternate path begins at the next byte and sets state 2, phase 1.
Two seven-entry sequences of player frames for the two facings, read at $8EA8.
The seven turning frames for the second facing. The door exit routine also uses this location as a biased lookup base.
Four frame codes for entering a door when the facing byte has bit 7 set.
Four frame codes for entering a door when the facing byte has bit 7 clear. The following byte begins the phase-indexed door frame lookup.
Phase-indexed animation codes. Entry phases 7 through 12 read this area through $90B3.
Three frame codes reached by $9116 in the first half of the visible doorway exit.
Three final frame codes reached by $9116 before the door handler tests the scene transition.
Door-transition workspace explicitly cleared at the state entry $9053.
Enters state 4, clears its phase and $9052, and requests effect 7.

During phases 0 to 3, attempts a one-unit step toward the center of the angular cell, but advances the animation even if geometry rejects the step. Later phases hide and reveal the player. The test at $9125 requires $170B to equal 3 for the collapse path.
Concealed-door motion counter. The animation advances its phase only on every second update of this counter.
Countdown set by the concealed summit-door path and decremented while that path waits before advancing the scene.
Hides the player once the doorway animation reaches phase $0D. A summit flag starts a timed pause that signals completion. The regular route moves the hidden player around the tower before emerging.
Uses the reversed phase count and facing to select a frame from the paired opening animation tables.
Immediate operand used when selecting the reverse doorway animation frame.
Enters state 5 only if the shot slot at $9B contains $FF, then resets the animation phase and requests sound $0F.
Sets the sprite frame from $904B and the facing bit. On animation phase 1 it initializes the projectile before resetting the state after phase 3.
Copies player height into the shot slot, chooses the initial angle one step to either side of $C6, marks the slot active and records its signed direction from the facing bit.
Signed vertical direction captured on entering lift motion. The lift update uses it to form the vertical delta.
Saves the requested vertical direction, enters state 6 with its phase reset and releases a matching pending floor change through $B13F.
Centers the player in the current angular cell before updating the lift and player height through the selected direction.
Attempts a collision against the four slots using the player's current angle and height, then checks special states and relative height before returning.
Checks the visible player against the object slots and adjusts motion or changes player state when the contact path wins.
Falling-player phase threshold. The object/geometry collision decision chooses $0F or $14 before entering the fall.
Enters player state 7, clears its phase and result flag, subtracts two technique points and requests sound $0B.
Sixteen signed height increments for early falling phases. The handler at $93AB caps its lookup at index 15.

Selects a facing-relative animation frame and adds the signed vertical displacement at $9380. After the initial phase it moves downward in four-unit steps and checks for landing or crossing zero height.
Sets state 8 and zero height, changes or clears active object slots, resets sound and queues effects $0C and $0D.
Steps the phase counter and selects a sprite frame from its quarter speed value for the first $18 phases.
Sets state 9, seeds the phase counter with $FF and resets the SID before collapse updates.
In the descending phase, lowers the player and shifts each of the sixteen map columns down a tile beginning near the visible height. The six-row threshold chooses the last collapse phase.
Eight colour registers initialized at $9575 during the collapse animation.
Sprite frame pointers copied into the collapse animation staging bytes at $9570. Its last two entries are initialized by the setup.
Frame-pointer slot 6 in the collapse pointer table, initialized to $17 and changed by the animation.
Frame-pointer slot 7 in the collapse pointer table, initialized to $16 before staging the debris.
Horizontal offsets from the debris group's base X, used by the per-sprite position loop.
Fourth collapse sprite's X offset from the group's base. The setup initializes it to $18 before the animation.
Vertical offsets relative to the collapse animation's moving base Y, added by the loop at $958D.
Vertical offset slot 6, initialized with the companion offset at $9517 and advanced during the collapse.
Vertical offset slot 7, adjusted as the paired lower sprites move during the collapse.
Base X coordinate to which the collapse sprite offsets at $9508 are added.
Base Y coordinate added to each debris sprite's relative Y. The animation updates it as the group falls.
Phase index used to select the debris motion path. The collapse code advances it after each segment.
Restores base sprite shapes, positions eight debris sprites and advances their X and Y spread with display ticks while queuing successive collapse effects.
Marks the projectile slot as free and clears its render state.
Indexed increments added to the projectile height during its active movement phases.

Advances the shot along the circumference, applies its height-change table and tests the scenery and object slots. Changes the struck slot or starts the projectile's ending phase according to the result.
Clears the four type bytes at $9C-$9F so those shared object slots begin inactive.

Derives the draw height at $68-$69 from $45-$46 minus eight and the threshold at $6A-$6B from $45-$46 plus $4D. Applies a wrap correction to the lower coordinate before updating object visibility and order.
Passes the four main object slots and a fifth slot to $A9B7. The fifth gets the blank pointer $9A when its phase is $FF.
Compares the four projected object positions to build a six-bit ordering index for assigning sprite slots.
Maps the six pairwise sprite-coordinate comparisons in X to four packed two-bit indices. The sorter adds 4 to each index to allocate VIC slots 4 through 7.
Object slot index saved at the start of a four-slot update and restored after subroutines change Y.
Signed increments for the object movement path at $99A5. A zero entry skips the incremental height adjustment.
Object angle before the attempted horizontal step. It is restored when map or object overlap rejects the motion.
Saved low height byte for an object motion attempt, available to restore after a blocked step.
Saved high byte of the object's height, paired with $97FB for position rollback.
Signed vertical displacement used by the timed object-motion path.
Four entries select the alternating colour during an object's short timed colour animation.

Visits slots 3 down to 0 by $9C type. Type 7 animates and moves along the circumference. Type 5 times a transition to type 2. Other active slots check geometry and update movement before the shared next-slot tail.
Advances the current object's vertical or contact state, checking the map and the other slots before selecting a new phase.
Sign extension operand for the high-byte addition of the object's signed vertical increment.
Continues the height update with wrap and collision recovery. The following paths can restore the old coordinates and change slot state or chase direction.
First slot of the object overlap candidate pair. The overlap filter uses it to select the appropriate mask.
Other object slot in the candidate pair, returned in X when the overlap is accepted.
Fifteen rows of accepted horizontal offsets for the general object overlap test. The selected row must contain the column bit from $9AE0.
Single-bit values for selecting a column from the two 15-row masks alongside this table.
Fifteen rows checked in the special slot-4 overlap path at $9B73. Empty outer rows reject large vertical separations.
Tests a candidate object's angular distance and height against the active object slots, reporting a matching slot in X when the overlap checks pass.
Patched initial mask column in the overlap probe. X selects a bit from $9AE0.
Tests the candidate slot against one of two class mask tables and returns the matching pair, or continues the earlier search.
Object slot saved across calls by the contact routine beginning at $9B92.
Builds a probe from the object's signed motion and current position. Uses the return value to select the advance, reverse or fall path.
Selected object slot retained across drawing and screen projection calls.
Sixteen computed column offsets refreshed each draw from $9CDC and the current player angle.
Projects sixteen angular columns, then compares each slot's height to the drawing bounds. Hides or retires out-of-range slots and passes visible slots to $9DBA.
Wraps the supplied angle after adding $20 and subtracting the player's angle $C6. Returns the 0-to-127 index in X and its projected value from $C980 in A.
Maps the angular difference from the player into the folded depth value used for sprite ordering.
Patched subtrahend in the final height subtraction at $9D05.
First byte of the three-byte mask contribution for each relative tower column.
Second mask byte merged when an object draws behind the edge of a tile.
Third mask byte for the same occlusion class selected at $9F99.
Current map column in the object occlusion loop, updated as the loop advances around the tower.
First map column to scan for tile masks affecting the selected object.
End column of the object occlusion scan, compared with the incremented column modulo 16.
Flag accumulated during the mask scan and tested to decide whether to apply the sprite masks.
Number of three-byte mask repetitions for the top band of an object sprite, indexed by its alignment.
Eight three-byte repetitions for the middle sprite band at each alignment.
Number of repetitions in the bottom mask band, complementing the top band's count.
Horizontal projection reference subtracted from the map column's projected display position.
Low two alignment bits used to select the lengths of the three sprite mask bands.
Object angle divided by eight before adding the two tile scan offsets.
Maps a projected X column to the initial three-byte mask index. $FF values reject the column.
Converts both nybbles of the object's width and alignment byte into angular bounds, iterates columns with a 16-column wrap, and uses carry to report special states or a rendered overlay.
Applies three patched AND masks to successive frame bytes, repeating the triplet X times and advancing Y for each byte.
Patched low source address for the first frame byte in a mask group. The following store uses the separately patched destination at $9F11-$9F12.
Patched high address of the frame byte load for position 1 of the three-byte group.
Patched AND mask applied to the frame byte for position 1 of the three-byte group.
Patched low address of the masked frame byte store for position 1 of the three-byte group.
Patched high address from the frame pointer table for the first sprite-mask write.
Patched low source address for the second frame byte. The masked result goes to the distinct destination at $9F1A-$9F1B.
Patched high address of the frame byte load for position 2 of the three-byte group.
Patched AND mask applied to the frame byte for position 2 of the three-byte group.
